pll2d9c1-d1e3514.summary: Turns to the orders of angels, which Scripture names as nine: Angels, Archangels, Principalities, Powers, Virtues, Dominations, Thrones, Cherubim, Seraphim.

pll2d9c1-d1e3526.summary: Notes that the orders form three groups of three, impressing a likeness of the Trinity, and gives Dionysius's arrangement: highest Seraphim, Cherubim, Thrones; middle Dominations, Principalities, Powers; lowest Virtues, Archangels, Angels.

pl-l2d9c1.summary: Introduces the angelic orders: Scripture names nine (Angels, Archangels, Principalities, Powers, Virtues, Dominations, Thrones, Cherubim, Seraphim), arranged in three groups of three as an impressed likeness of the Trinity. Dionysius: highest Seraphim, Cherubim, Thrones; middle Dominations, Principalities, Powers; lowest Virtues, Archangels, Angels.
claims: There are nine orders of angels.
They form three groups of three, reflecting the Trinity.
Dionysius places Seraphim, Cherubim, Thrones highest; Dominations, Principalities, Powers in the middle; Virtues, Archangels, Angels lowest.
